A bike chain wears out faster when left dry because the metal links lack the essential lubrication that reduces friction and prevents corrosion. Without oil or grease, the microscopic teeth on the chain and the corresponding cogs grind directly against each other, creating excessive heat and accelerating the wear of the metal. This friction also allows dirt and grit to act like sandpaper, embedding itself between the links and causing rapid degradation. Over time, a dry chain will stretch, skip gears, and eventually snap, leading to costly repairs for the customer.
